transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Refrigerant systems are sealed under high pressure; adding gas without finding and fixing the leak is dangerous, illegal in many contexts, and will not fix the problem because the underlying fault (like a blockage or component failure) remains. Since both compartments are warm but the compressor is running and hot at the back, we need to distinguish between a lack of cooling production (sealed system) and a failure to move the cold air around. The most common cause for this specific pattern on frost-free models is actually not a gas leak, but ice blocking the airflow. To narrow this down: Is the freezer compartment still cold or freezing while only the fridge section is warm? If the freezer is also warm, it points more strongly to a sealed system issue. If the freezer is still cold, we are likely looking at an airflow blockage (like iced-up coils) which is often repairable.
freezer is warm too, about 0C and everything has thawed. fridge is about 13C. compressor runs non stop and the back is only barely warm tho

Since both the freezer and fridge are warm (0°C and 13°C respectively) and the compressor is running continuously but only getting 'barely' warm at the back, this points to a failure in the sealed cooling system. The refrigerant has likely leaked out or there is a blockage in the capillary tubes. These systems are hermetically sealed under high pressure and often use flammable gases (like R600a). Attempting to open them yourself is dangerous, illegal for a non-certified person, and will not work because the gas will simply leak out again unless the source of the leak is found and repaired by specialist equipment. Furthermore, if there is a blockage inside the system, adding more gas will do nothing. Before we accept that it needs an engineer, please check one simple thing: ensure the condenser coils (usually a black grille at the back or underneath) are not covered in dust or lint and that there is at least 5cm of space around them. If they are clean and ventilated, the issue is probably internal. Given the symptoms, this will require a qualified refrigeration engineer to diagnose and repair (or replace the unit if the repair cost is high). Please do not attempt any DIY fixes on the cooling circuit.

not sure what the condenser looks like on this one, cant really see a grille at the back. its an indesit and the plate says R600a if that helps. is there anything else i can try myself before paying an engineer, its out of warranty and i want the cheapest option

No. Do not buy a regas kit. 1. It is illegal and dangerous for anyone without F-Gas certification to handle R600a gas. It is highly flammable and pressurised; piercing the pipes can cause fire or explosion.
2. The system is sealed. If it has lost its gas, there is a leak. A DIY kit cannot find or fix a microscopic leak in copper tubing buried inside insulation. Even if you added gas, it would just leak out again within days.
3. This is typical of a lack of refrigerant or a blockage in the capillary tubes. Neither can be fixed by adding gas. The cheapest option, given that it is out of warranty and the sealed system has failed, is usually to replace the appliance. Repairing a sealed system requires specialist recovery equipment, leak detection tools, vacuum pumps, and precise weighing of gas—equipment that costs thousands of pounds. Most engineers will not attempt a repair on an older Indesit because the labour cost often exceeds the value of the fridge-freezer. Please unplug the unit to save electricity while it runs uselessly, and contact a qualified refrigeration engineer for a final confirmation (or simply start looking at replacements).
